title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: an unmanaged rename refuses a stray-object package and a declared namespace its object names do not carry
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"huangyiirene"} -->
_Requested by **Irene** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TJXtQ1tVD26ecLDZxFS67x?thread=cmsg_01TJXtQ1tVD26ecLDZxFS67x8Be2AAcUBhodBsvnWLd3Xs)_
Part of #36166

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: #36166 comment 7146137652
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` teaches the unmanaged install's `targetNamespace` rename (`git grep` of `skills/` for `targetNamespace`, `rename-on-install` and `unmanaged`: zero hits at a73edb3c; control: `namespace` hits `skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md` six times)

Seat: repo:objectstack#2 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAjMiYmA3shv2bCSnaS

> **Declaration ruled.** The maintainer chose 「B 照 #36138 先例声明为 patch」 (seat record `Ruling-ref: #36166 comment 7146137652`): the changeset is `patch` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, the same pair as #36138's changeset. No `packages/spec` entry is written. The diff changes the answer an install request gets, not what a metadata author can write.

## 维护者速读

- 以不托管方式安装应用包并指定新命名空间的人:原来有两种包会被静默拼成双前缀的对象名,现在安装前就拒绝并说明原因;只有一个对象的包照旧改名。
- 属于"应用包安装与命名"这条线,接续上一轮已合并的双前缀拒绝修复。
- 碰到这两种包的安装者会看到明确的拒绝,不再得到三种拼写混杂的副本;改法是在包上声明命名空间,随时可撤回本改动。
- 无。

## What changes

`planUnmanagedImport` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts`), on the rename path only (a `targetNamespace` that differs from the source namespace). Each of the card's three cases now has an answer, and a test pins each one:

1. **Single object, namespace-less (`demoasset_asset` alone): stays as the ADR-0048 §3.5 rename.** One name carries no signal; the planner docblock already says a single name cannot tell a two-word short name from a foreign prefix. The pin keeps its assertion. Its title now states the decision: `DECIDED: a single-object package keeps the ADR rename, foreign prefix or not`.
2. **A stray object beside a shared prefix (`demoasset_asset`, `demoasset_site`, `site`): refused.** `derivedNamespaceContradiction` now groups object names by first segment. When no object carries the derived prefix, every group of two or more is refused at its own names. The stray is in no entry and does not lift the refusal. Before this, the `every(...)` early return let one stray turn the signal off.
3. **A declared `namespace` the object names do not carry (`namespace: 'other'`, `demoasset_*`): refused.** The new `declaredNamespaceContradiction` asks the one prefix judge, `validateObjectNamespacePrefix` (`@objectstack/spec/kernel`), the same judge `defineStack`, the publish pre-flight and the save door ask. Each object it refuses is named.

Both refusals use the existing `unmanagedInstallRenameRefusal` envelope (`400 INVALID_REQUEST`, `details.targetNamespace`, `details.refused` with one object entry each, its `reason` naming the namespace in play and the prefix). They are raised before the base exists. ADR-0129 D2 and ADR-0048 §3.5 ids stay on the docblocks.

**Mechanism assumptions, as measured** (scratch probe at a73edb3c, deleted afterwards):
- PM assumption 1 (case 3 without a rename refuses at the save door): **holds**. `importUnmanagedPackage` with no `targetNamespace` answers `NAMESPACE_PREFIX/422`. But the same probe shows the save door also refuses the honest namespace-less `purchase_order` without a rename (`NAMESPACE_PREFIX/422`), a name the ADR rename turns into an install that works. So "the two doors agree" does not tell the cases apart. The fact that does is the judge's own skip: a package with no `namespace` is the legacy shape whose objects are not judged, while a declared one is held to its prefix at every authoring door. Case 3 is refused on that basis, and a test pins the save-door agreement as a CONTROL.
- PM assumption 2 (the group signal): **holds**. No CONTROL changes answer: `purchase_order`+`asset_owner` share nothing, `asset`+`site` have no segment, and one object carrying the derived prefix still clears it. `purchase_order`+`purchase_item`+`vendor` is now refused (`purchase_order`, `purchase_item` named). Without `vendor` it was already refused by #36138.
- PM assumption 3 (case 1 stays as the rename): **holds**, as decided above.

Contract-review fix round (record 7154567814 on this PR): the refusal for a group that is not the whole package now ends by asking for every other object to be named under the declared namespace too, since declaring the group's prefix alone would be refused on the next attempt (S2); a whole-package group keeps #36138's sentence. `content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx` now teaches the new answers: the in-front rename holds for a package that declares no `namespace`, the group row no longer needs every object name, and a new row covers a declared `namespace` the object names do not carry (S1). The changeset names the bare-name case and its closing remedy is "declare `namespace` and name every object under it" (S1, S2). A test with two refused groups in one body pins the refused names in manifest order (N4), and the docblock says the stray is refused by the save door too (N1).

Fixture triage, same file: `refuses an object whose copy name another object's copy claims` built its collision from a bare `lead` under a declared `crm`, which case 3 now refuses first. Its fixture drops `namespace` (so `crm` is derived from `com.example.crm`), and it still pins the collision branch, which namespace-less bodies still reach. The new declared-namespace test also pins a bare name under a declared namespace as refused.

## ADR note owed

Carrier: #36166 itself. It stays open under `Part of` until the ADR-0048 §3.5 dated note (and the case-1 decision) lands as an add-only governed docs/adr PR, which carries the closing line for #36166. (The earlier "ADR revisions" rolling card #36086 closed on 2026-11-24.)

> **Note (2026-11-24, #36166, following #35823 / PR #36138)** — on §3.5's rename sentence "a name that lacks the package's prefix takes it in front". On the unmanaged rename path that sentence now has three bounds. (1) A package that declares no `namespace` is refused, not renamed, when no object name carries the namespace derived from its id and two or more object names share a first segment: each object of each such group is refused (`400 INVALID_REQUEST`), whether every object shares the segment (#36138) or a stray object stands beside the group (#36166). So two-word short names the package repeats (`purchase_order` beside `purchase_item`) are refused too, and declaring `namespace` lifts the refusal. (2) A package that declares a `namespace` is refused for each object name the namespace-prefix judge (`validateObjectNamespacePrefix`) refuses under it. The rename has no declared prefix in such a name to replace, and every authoring door already refuses that name. (3) Decided to stay as written: a namespace-less package's single object, foreign prefix or not (`demoasset_asset` alone copies as `TARGET_demoasset_asset`), because one name cannot tell a two-word short name from a foreign prefix. Namespace-less object names that share no first segment (`purchase_order` beside `asset_owner`, bare `asset` beside `site`) also stay as written. A body that writes the id-derived namespace out as `namespace` is judged as declared, so bound (2) applies to it and the shapes in (3) are refused for it. Pinned in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.test.ts`.

## Tests

- `package-unmanaged-install.test.ts`: four new refusal tests: the stray-object plan and the verb with zero writes; the repeated two-word short name with and without a stray, and the declared control; the declared-namespace plan, partial and bare cases, and the verb with zero writes (`writes`, `packages`, `sys_metadata` empty). One new CONTROL (the save door agrees without a rename). One CONTROL retitled `DECIDED`. The declared CONTROL keeps its `namespace: 'demoasset'` half and loses the `other` half, now a refusal. Refusal tests assert `status` + `code` and the `details.refused` names. The only prose they check is the namespace named in `reason`.

<details><summary>Test runs (first round at tree 710745f8; the fix-round head c4494a60 re-ran below)</summary>

- At c4494a60, after building the metadata-protocol closure under the verify lock: target file `Tests 113 passed (113)`; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` `Test Files 370 passed | 9 skipped (379)`, `Tests 23420 passed | 45 skipped (23465)`; `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) exit 0; `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The S2 change alters only the remedy sentence, which no test asserts (refusal tests assert status, code and refused names), so no ablation was owed for it.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` (under the verify lock): `Test Files 369 passed | 9 skipped (378)`, `Tests 23396 passed | 45 skipped (23441)`; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- Consumer sweep (the rename's callers with real fixtures): `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/protocol-unmanaged-import-rename-battery.test.ts src/protocol-package-lifecycle.test.ts`, after a rebuild of objectql's closure that includes `metadata-protocol` (`dist/index.js` carries `declaredNamespaceContradiction`): `Tests 22 passed (22)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The cloud-connection install-local tests stub the importer. The dogfood and runtime callers use `duplicatePackage`, which is not touched.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (committed first; `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restore = HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty)</summary>

- Case 2: the group-size guard (skip a group of fewer than two names) gained a second clause that also skips any group smaller than the whole object set, which puts the old every-or-nothing hole back. The mutation landed (anchor 1 to 0, blob b6525739 to 50f7c2b9). Red: `Tests 3 failed | 109 passed (112)`, the stray-object plan, the stray-object verb and the repeated short name with a stray. Restored: blob b6525739 == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Case 3: anchor `: declaredNamespaceContradiction(sourcePackageId, declaredNamespace, namespace, objectNames);` replaced with `: undefined;`. The mutation landed (blob b6525739 to ce8284d8). Red: `Tests 3 failed | 109 passed (112)`, the three declared-namespace refusal tests. Restored: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Green before and after: `Tests 112 passed (112)`.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- `content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx` is the one hand-written page that teaches this rename; it is updated in this PR (contract-review S1). No skill teaches it (see `Skills-docs:`).
- The refusal does not add `details.derivedNamespace` / `details.commonPrefix` keys. Each `reason` names them, as the #36138 envelope does. Adding keys would change the envelope's shape, which this card does not own.

## Verification

<details><summary>Readings at the head c4494a60c2a194d7b4e872b39482ff00a9310b51</summary>

- Derived gates at c4494a60 (`dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 95 families; `--ran` with exit codes: 95 derived, 91 run, 4 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun): all 91 exit 0, including `check:doc-authoring`, `check-changeset-no-major --base origin/main`, `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`, `check-empty-changeset --base origin/main`, `check:nul-bytes`, the docs-section and ADR-link families the page edit adds, and `check:liveness`. NOT MEASURED (exit 3, prerequisite missing in this checkout; CI builds them): `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:skill-examples` (client SDK not built) and `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (needs an unshallow clone). `overlap-check`: VERDICT clean exit 0 against origin/main a386a1d8.
- PR check-runs at c4494a60, all completed: 40 success, 15 skipped by their selectors, 0 failed. The successes include every required context in play: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core and Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Live E2E UI, Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, plus Check Changeset, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links and Spec property liveness.
- **Full dogfood battery at c4494a60c2a194d7b4e872b39482ff00a9310b51** (owed by the `(narrowing)` arm): `git rev-parse HEAD` = c4494a60 before and after, clean tree. Dogfood closure built under the verify lock (VERDICT command-exit 0), then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` with no shard and no path: `Test Files 487 passed | 3 skipped (490)`, `Tests 4128 passed | 68 skipped (4196)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0` (held 2175s), no failures.
- Earlier readings, superseded: c171abb9 `Tests 4128 passed | 68 skipped (4196)`; 1188c47a `Tests 4127 passed | 68 skipped (4195)`.
- Accepted deviation (contract-review N2, inherited from #36138's signal): on the namespace-less path, two or more `sys_*` object names form a group and are refused with "declare `namespace`", while the declared path's judge exempts `sys_*`. Left as it is; only the stray case is new in this PR.
</details>

**Read first:** (1) `declaredNamespaceContradiction`: is the prefix judge the right predicate for refusing a declared-namespace object? (2) `derivedNamespaceContradiction`'s grouping loop: does any group of two or more refuse an honest package you care about? (3) The retitled `DECIDED` single-object pin.

**Two-minute verification:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/package-unmanaged-install.test.ts` shows `Tests 112 passed (112)`.
